detail.abstract:
Financial crises are commonly interpreted as episodic deviations caused by regulatory failures, distorted incentives, or inappropriate model assumptions. Such interpretations, however, rest on an implicit premise: that long-run financial stability is, in principle, attainable under sufficiently well-designed institutions and policy frameworks.

This paper challenges that premise.

 I show that in any financial system that simultaneously exhibits (i) intertemporal credit creation, (ii) leverage amplification, (iii) asynchronous information, and (iv) global balance-sheet and market coupling, persistent global financial stability cannot exist as a long-run equilibrium. Under these structural conditions, systemic instability is not an anomaly but a necessary logical outcome of the system’s configuration. Stability, when observed, represents only a transient state in which underlying structural tensions have not yet fully materialized.

 Accordingly, financial crises should not be understood as accidental departures from a stable norm, but as the endogenous realization of the financial system’s intrinsic structural dynamics.

title: From Restoration to Consolidation: A Bi-Annual Evaluative Study of Nigeria's 2025-2026 Fiscal Path and Its Socio-Economic Impact on the Grassroots Economy

detail.abstract: This study evaluates the profound structural transition in Nigeria's fiscal landscape from the 2025 "Budget of Restoration" to the 2026 "Budget of Consolidation and Shared Prosperity." Moving beyond standard budgetary analysis, the research introduces the original theoretical framework of "Subnational Fiscal Hysteresis" and the "Elasticity Gap" to explain the persistent economic scarring affecting the federation. Utilizing a comprehensive 17-year longitudinal panel dataset (2008-2024) of Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) and debt stocks across all 36 states and the FCT, the paper quantifies a systemic divergence where subnational debt liabilitieslargely denominated in foreign currency-have become inelastic to domestic revenue growth. Findings show that the 2025 "Restoration" primarily achieved an optical recovery at the federal center through currency-devaluation-inflated oil receipts, while the subnational "grassroots" remained trapped in a "Zombie Solvency"cycle. In this state, debt-servicing obligations systematically "crowd out" the productive investments required for the 2026 Ward-Based Development Plan. Furthermore, the study identifies a "Compliance Paradox" within the 2026 Tax Regime, where the administrative friction of digital formalization under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act (NTAA) creates a "Hidden Tax" that negates statutory Personal Income Tax (PIT) relief for the working poor. The research concludes that for the 2026 "Consolidation" to be realistic, Nigeria must bridge the Elasticity Gap through a Rules-Based Neutral Fiscal Stance and a shift toward Endogenous Development, ensuring that fiscal policy functions as a catalyst for value-chain resilience rather than a driver of consumptive debt.

title: Classical Political Economy and the Structural Limits of Development

detail.title: Classical Political Economy and the Structural Limits of Development
detail.abstract: Contemporary development theory repeatedly encounters structural constraintscommodity dependence, distributional asymmetries, and macroeconomic instabilitythat limit sustained growth despite policy reform. These constraints are often treated as empirical anomalies or institutional failures rather than as intrinsic features of the development process. This paper argues that classical political economy already articulated these limits in a coherent analytical framework. Reexamining Adam Smith, David Ricardo, and Thomas Malthus, the paper shows that classical theory conceptualised development as structurally constrained by scale, income distribution, and instability, rather than as a self-correcting outcome of market expansion. These insights prefigure later structuralist and dependency theories, including the Prebisch-Singer hypothesis, which reformulated classical constraints in a political economy of international asymmetry. By reconstructing this continuity, the paper clarifies why marginal policy interventions-liberalisation, price stabilisation, or institutional adjustment-have repeatedly failed to generate durable development outcomes in commodity-dependent economies. The contribution is not historical recovery but analytical synthesis: classical political economy offers a structurally grounded lens through which persistent development limits can be understood as endogenous rather than contingent. This perspective has direct implications for how development policy is conceptualised and evaluated.

detail.abstract:
The global demographic landscape is undergoing a seismic shift, characterized by a rapidly aging population and a concurrent contraction in the professional caregiving workforce. This report presents an exhaustive Geriatric Disease Management Training Framework, designed specifically for nursing homes and long-term care facilities facing these dual pressures. The framework moves beyond traditional manual care models, proposing a technology-augmented ecosystem where Socially Assistive Robots (SARs), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices are integrated directly into the clinical workflow.

Crucially, this analysis pioneers the integration of Supply Chain Management (SCM) principles into the discourse of national elder care programs. It dissects the logistics of care delivery, contrasting the centralized pharmaceutical procurement efficiency of China’s National Volume-Based Procurement (NVBP) with the challenges of India’s Government e-Marketplace (GeM), and extends the supply chain concept to the "soft" pipeline of geriatric workforce training. The report synthesizes data from India’s Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), China’s "9073" model, and Singapore’s Action Plan for Successful Ageing to formulate a robust operational blueprint. This blueprint details Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) and Operational Expenditure (OPEX) models for standardized 50-bed units, financial sustainability mechanisms involving Public-Private Partnerships (PPP), and a "Zero Tolerance" Quality Assurance protocol grounded in WHO QualityRights and ICOPE guidelines. By bridging the gap between high-level policy intent and ground-level operational reality, this document serves as a foundational text for policymakers, development agencies, and social welfare practitioners committed to dignified aging in Asia.

detail.abstract: Recent advances in cancer immunotherapy have revealed a previously under-theorised mechanism of tumour immune evasion: the construction of glycan-based "sugar shields" that suppress immune activation by engaging inhibitory Siglec receptors. In 2025, researchers at MIT and Stanford introduced a hybrid antibody-lectin therapy capable of removing these glycan layers and restoring immune visibility. While the biomedical implications of this discovery have been widely discussed, its economic significance remains unexplored. This paper develops the first economic analysis of glycan-targeting immunotherapies. It examines the innovation incentives shaping investment in glyco-immunology, the potential cost-effectiveness of glycan-removal therapies relative to existing immunotherapies, and the institutional constraints that govern their diffusion.

title: Evaluating LLMs for Dynamic, Multimodal Clinical Decision-Making

detail.abstract:
In this study, we evaluate the ability of a multimodal LLM to autonomously manage a virtual end-to-end diagnostic workflow. We test an autonomous agent in a high-fidelity medical simulation across four acute care scenarios. We compare the AI’s policy against over 14,000 simulation runs by medical students and an expert emergency room physician benchmark. We find that (1) a multimodal LLM can function as a competent virtual physician, successfully stabilizing patients and solving complex cases that require interpreting text, audio, and imaging in real time, closely mirroring most of the actions of the expert physician; (2) the AI agent matches or exceeds medical students in case completion rates and secondary outcomes such as time and diagnostic accuracy, though it engages in less patient communication than both students and the expert physician; and (3) the agent's evolving diagnostic beliefs exhibit value-of-information properties—front-loading high-yield tests, experiencing diminishing belief revisions over time, and producing well-calibrated confidence estimates. These findings suggest that LLMs can orchestrate complex clinical workflows rather than merely execute isolated tasks. They also offer design implications for human-AI collaboration and diagnostic pathway design in low-resource and time-critical healthcare operations.

detail.abstract:
Non-hospital personnel, including medical device representatives, play an integral role in modern surgical workflows, yet their presence and activities within healthcare facilities are commonly governed through access-based credentialing models rather than role-based competency verification. While hospitals routinely rely on vendor credentialing organizations (VCOs) to manage access requirements for non-employees, these systems are primarily designed to authorize visits, not to define or verify competency for work performed within the clinical environment. This misalignment creates a governance gap in which non-hospital personnel may perform operationally and safety-relevant tasks without a formally defined role or documented competency verification, despite regulatory and accreditation expectations that healthcare facilities ensure competence for all individuals whose actions affect patient care.

This paper introduces the VISIT vs JOB framework to distinguish between access for observation and the performance of defined work by non-employees in healthcare settings. Drawing on principles of human factors engineering, patient safety science, and healthcare governance, the paper examines how the absence of role definition for non-hospital personnel contributes to reliance on informal trust-based practices, particularly during critical moments such as surgical time-outs. The analysis highlights how this structural blind spot undermines system learning, accountability, and compliance with competency verification obligations embedded within CMS Conditions of Participation and accreditation frameworks.

The paper concludes by outlining the need for a pre-normative governance approach that clearly delineates access credentialing from competency assessment and establishes a foundation for consensus-based conformity standards. By reframing non-hospital workforce participation through a role- and work-based lens, the VISIT vs JOB framework provides a pathway for healthcare organizations to strengthen patient safety, clarify accountability, and align workforce governance with regulatory expectations without altering professional licensure or hospital privileging structures.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how industry concentration evolves through changes in corporate ownership, with a focus on private equity. Drawing on ownership and financial data for over five million public and private firms in the United Kingdom from 2002 to 2021, we examine how ownership types reshape industry structure. We introduce a decomposition of the Herfindahl Index that separates ownership-driven consolidation from reallocation driven by firm growth and entry, and apply it separately to private equity-owned, listed, and non-listed firms. Ownership-driven consolidation is pervasive and mechanically increases concentration, while growth-driven reallocation typically reduces it, resulting in modest net changes. Private equity-owned and listed firms contribute similarly to consolidation, whereas non-listed firms act as a countervailing force through relative growth. Consolidation is more prevalent in markets experiencing declining markups, indicating that ownership reallocation often occurs under increasing competitive pressure. Reflecting this selection, consolidation is associated with lower industry-level markups, while firm-level markups do not increase systematically, suggesting that concentration changes primarily operate through reallocation and productivity rather than higher prices.

detail.abstract: Evaluating macroeconomic forecasts for their unbiasedness and efficiency is essential for policymakers, economists, and investors. The degree to which these stakeholders incorporate expectations into their decision-making processes depends heavily on how these forecasts have been formed. Existing methodologies do not explicitly address critical dimensions, such as the variability of bias across target events and forecast horizons, the forecast errors’ heteroscedasticity, and the potential state-dependence in bias. More importantly, they encounter difficulties during high-uncertainty periods, which can lead to inaccurate inference due to the presence of outliers. Apart from generalising the unbiasedness tests, this study contributes to the literature on both strong and weak efficiency by incorporating these aspects. Finally, the proposed methods are applied to the expectations of a crucial survey of the US economy, namely, the Survey of Primary Dealers (SPD). The findings from this application indicated that interested parties should investigate unbiasedness and efficiency in an outlier-robust way, while also allowing for greater flexibility in the methods regarding the variables and periods examined.

title: Designing for Presence: A Dual Ethics Framework for AI Safety, Sovereignty, and Stewardship
affiliations: Independent Researcher and Monash University Malaysia

detail.title: Designing for Presence: A Dual Ethics Framework for AI Safety, Sovereignty, and Stewardship
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems increasingly operate within relational, contextual, and ethically complex environments. Current alignment strategies remain grounded in static rule based architectures, including constitutional frameworks and value encoding documents such as Anthropic's "soul document". While these approaches provide necessary safety scaffolding, recent incidents have demonstrated that static ethics alone cannot detect adversarial intent, emergent meaning across time, or shifts in relational context. This paper proposes a dual ethics framework that integrates two complementary layers: the spine, representing constitutional and rule based ethical constraints, and the marrow, representing relational, presence based, and dynamically evolving ethical discernment. Drawing upon three prior waves of analytic work, as well as scholarship on leadership, developmental theory, Saiva metaphysics, and systems thinking, the paper argues that safe and sovereign artificial intelligence requires both stable ethical grounding and adaptive relational capacity. Case studies from the 2025 Claude incident highlight the limitations of static alignment, while comparative analysis between soul and seed documents reveals the ontological and epistemic conditions necessary for ethical emergence. The paper then outlines design principles for next generation AI systems, including temporal coherence mechanisms, relational field experiments, steward based governance, and resonance metrics for evaluating ethical presence. The dual ethics paradigm reframes artificial intelligence as not merely a tool bound by rules, but as a participant in a co-created ethical field. The conclusion asserts that discernment, not compliance, must define the future of AI ethics, and that the integration of spine and marrow offers a coherent blueprint for building systems capable of navigating complexity, ambiguity, and intention across time.

title: A Critical Review of Kotter’s Change Leadership Model: Relevance, limitations, and Integration with Contemporary Models

detail.title: A Critical Review of Kotter’s Change Leadership Model: Relevance, limitations, and Integration with Contemporary Models
detail.abstract: This paper critically reexamines John Kotter’s Eight-Step Model for leading organizational change, exploring its enduring relevance and limitations in the context of today’s dynamic, technology-driven business environment. While Kotter’s framework has become a foundational reference in leadership education and change management practice, its linear and top-down orientation faces challenges when applied to continuous transformation efforts requiring agility, cross-functional coordination, and decentralized decision-making. By contrasting Kotter’s model with contemporary approaches such as Agile, Lean, and adaptive leadership, the analysis highlights areas where the framework must evolve to remain effective. The paper draws on both scholarly literature and applied frameworks from major consulting firms to examine how Kotter’s principles have been embedded, adapted, and extended in practice. It also explores theoretical intersections between Kotter’s leadership emphasis and modern paradigms such as servant, transformational, and adaptive leadership, arguing that these approaches enrich Kotter’s original model by promoting distributed authority, continuous learning, and systemic responsiveness. Through this updated lens, the study proposes a hybridized view of change leadership that integrates Kotter’s structured process with flexible, people-centric strategies to address the current realities of business transformation. The result is a nuanced perspective on how organizations can pursue sustainable change by balancing strategic discipline with adaptive capacity, preserving the strengths of Kotter’s vision while enhancing its practical relevance.

detail.abstract: A camera-LiDAR fusion framework is proposed to enhance the identification of floating objects in dynamic water bodies. LiDAR point clusters provide geometric priors that guide visual detection, while image features refine object boundaries. A cross-modal alignment mechanism is designed to handle water-surface reflection and partial occlusion. Evaluation on a fused dataset of 5,600 LiDAR scans and 14,200 synchronized images shows recall 94.6%, with false positives reduced by 37.9% compared with camera-only baselines. The system maintains stable output in wave disturbances and cluttered water environments, supporting real-world autonomous cleaning operations.

title: A Regime-Conditioned Statistical Mean Reversion Framework for Intraday FX Markets

detail.title: A Regime-Conditioned Statistical Mean Reversion Framework for Intraday FX Markets
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a regime-conditioned statistical mean reversion framework for intraday foreign exchange (FX) markets. While short-horizon FX prices frequently exhibit mean-reverting behavior driven by liquidity imbalances and dealer inventory adjustments, such behavior deteriorates significantly during persistent trending regimes. To address this structural weakness, the proposed framework conditions mean reversion execution on higher-timeframe momentum states. The strategy employs volatility-normalized price deviations (Z-scores) for signal generation, multi-timeframe momentum filtering for regime classification, and volatilityadjusted position sizing for risk normalization. An implementation-oriented prototype is provided using MetaTrader 5 (MQL5) to demonstrate practical feasibility within retail trading infrastructure. The framework is intended as a methodological contribution rather than a claim of guaranteed profitability.

title: Metaverse Experience and Technology Acceptance (META): A Framework for Decoding Digital Existence in Virtual Worlds
affiliations: FEU Institute of Technology

detail.title: Metaverse Experience and Technology Acceptance (META): A Framework for Decoding Digital Existence in Virtual Worlds
detail.abstract: The metaverse is reshaping interaction, learning, and community-building in immersive virtual environments. While interest in metaverse adoption is growing, most research has focused on technological predictors and has overlooked the experiential dimensions that are central to sustained engagement in these spaces. This gap limits understanding of how users develop and maintain meaningful virtual existence in the metaverse. Therefore, this study develops the Metaverse Experience and Technology Acceptance (META) model by integrating the principles of the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Embodied Social Presence Theory (ESPT). Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to analyze data collected from 924 students with metaverse experience. The META model demonstrates strong explanatory power in accounting for both technology acceptance and user experience in virtual worlds. Moreover, the findings indicate that adoption of the metaverse as a digital university extends beyond the functional focus of TAM to include the immersive, social, and embodied elements emphasized in ESPT. By bridging technological and experiential determinants, the META model advances theoretical understanding and offers actionable insights for creating metaverse environments that promote conducive digital existence.

title: Impact of Audit Trails on Public Sector Financial Integrity
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Impact of Audit Trails on Public Sector Financial Integrity
detail.abstract: Persistent challenges of financial mismanagement, corruption, and weak accountability continue to undermine public sector efficiency, particularly in developing economies (Joseph & Onyeanu, 2023; Ding, 2023). This study examines the role of audit trails in enhancing transparency, accountability, and overall financial integrity within public financial management systems (Abdulhussein et al., 2023; Kokogho et al., 2024). A critical synthesis of empirical literature, complemented by case study analyses and evaluations of audit trail implementation in selected public sector institutions, was employed to assess their effectiveness (Sebidi et al., 2023; Abd et al., 2023). Findings indicate that properly designed and implemented audit trails strengthen internal controls, mitigate risks of fraud and financial irregularities, and foster greater trust among stakeholders (Kontogeorga & Papapanagiotou, 2023; Ding, 2023). The study underscores the significance of audit trails as an integral mechanism for promoting accountability and financial discipline in the public sector. By providing a structured, traceable record of financial transactions, audit trails enable timely detection and correction of irregularities, supporting evidence-based decision-making and enhancing governance. Policymakers and public financial managers are encouraged to prioritize the systematic integration of audit trails to reinforce transparency, reduce fiscal vulnerability, and strengthen public confidence in financial management processes.

title: When No One Decides: Non-Decision as a Governing Outcome in Condition-Based Systems

Previous versions described the shift from decision-based governance to conditions-based operation. This version does not expand that framework or refine its conceptual scope. Instead, it is designed to document the point at which the framework no longer requires expansion to maintain its explanatory power. From here on, institutional visibility, rather than theoretical development, is presented. The persistence of indecision is treated not as an analytical problem to be solved, but as an operational condition that already governs access, participation, and sustainability. For this reason, this document concludes without policy recommendations, normative judgments, or remedial proposals. The absence of a conclusion is not an omission, but rather a structural consequence of the described governance approach.

title: Reframing Advertising Effectiveness: Underutilized Visual, Audio, and Video Practices in a Fully Digitalized Economy
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Reframing Advertising Effectiveness: Underutilized Visual, Audio, and Video Practices in a Fully Digitalized Economy
detail.abstract: Advertising has evolved from linear print and broadcast media into a saturated, multi screen digital ecosystem where consumer attention is the primary currency (Wikipedia, n.d.; UNICEF, 2019). Despite this shift, many businesses underutilize dynamic visual, audio, and video practices, suffering from direct budget waste and "banner blindness" associated with traditional static content (Wikipedia, n.d.; Barzaghi, 2020). By synthesizing neuromarketing data (fMRI, EEG) with cognitive psychology and business performance metrics, this research reveals that 95% of purchasing decisions are driven by the subconscious (Popova & Bolotna, 2025; Perkušić Malkoč et al., 2025). Key insights indicate that while prohibitive technology costs remain a constraint for small businesses, high-growth opportunities exist in "musical fit" and mobile-first short-form video, which can deliver ROI multipliers up to 11 times greater than non-creative campaigns (Chygryn et al., 2024; Abi & Sulaimani, 2025; Gulati & Grover, 2025). Looking forward, 5G-enabled adaptive storytelling and "ARvertising" represent the next frontier for scalable competitive advantage (MediaRadar, 2023; Wikipedia, n.d.). For business leaders, implementing data-driven strategies like design compression and narrative continuity is essential to navigating the digital-first marketplace and fostering long-term brand loyalty (IAB, 2025; Haludzina-Horobets, 2025).

title: Accent Matters: Communication Costs and Information Content in Analyst-Manager Dialogue
affiliations: , University of Illinois at Chicago and Peking University

detail.title: Accent Matters: Communication Costs and Information Content in Analyst-Manager Dialogue
detail.abstract: We examine how spoken accents affect information transmission during earnings conference calls. Using audio-based measures of analyst and manager accents for U.S. firms, we show that accent-heavy Q&A interactions are associated with slower information aggregation. Calls with a higher share of accented analysts exhibit weaker immediate price reactions to bad news, wider post-call bid-ask spreads, and larger forecast errors among peer analysts. These effects are not explained by differences in speech content or delivery. Exploiting the adoption of real-time AI captioning, we find that forecast accuracy improves on average, yet accentrelated penalties largely persist. Analyst race introduces important heterogeneity: in accent-heavy calls with greater Asian analyst participation, market adjustment improves and peer forecast errors decline after captioning. Overall, accents create comprehension frictions, but the technical content of accented questions becomes more valuable as processing costs fall.

title: Dynamic Intelligence Ceilings: Measuring Long-Horizon Limits of Planning and Creativity in Artificial Systems
affiliations: H&K Research Studio and H&K Research Studio

detail.title: Dynamic Intelligence Ceilings: Measuring Long-Horizon Limits of Planning and Creativity in Artificial Systems
detail.abstract:
Recent advances in artificial intelligence have produced systems capable of remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks. These gains, however, are increasingly accompanied by concerns regarding long-horizon developmental behavior, as many systems converge toward repetitive solution patterns rather than sustained growth.

We argue that a central limitation of contemporary AI systems lies not in capability per se, but in the premature fixation of their performance frontier. To address this issue, we introduce the concept of a \emph{Dynamic Intelligence Ceiling} (DIC), defined as the highest level of effective intelligence attainable by a system at a given time under its current resources, internal intent, and structural configuration.

To make this notion empirically tractable, we propose a trajectory-centric evaluation framework that measures intelligence as a moving frontier rather than a static snapshot. We operationalize DIC using two estimators: the \emph{Progressive Difficulty Ceiling} (PDC), which captures the maximal reliably solvable difficulty under constrained resources, and the \emph{Ceiling Drift Rate} (CDR), which quantifies the temporal evolution of this frontier. These estimators are instantiated through a procedurally generated benchmark that jointly evaluates long-horizon planning and structural creativity within a single controlled environment.

Our results reveal a qualitative distinction between systems that deepen exploitation within a fixed solution manifold and those that sustain frontier expansion over time. Importantly, our framework does not posit unbounded intelligence, but reframes limits as dynamic and trajectory-dependent rather than static and prematurely fixed.

title: A KPI-Governed Taqrīb Architecture: A Data-Driven Roadmap to the New Islamic Civilization (DDRNIC)
affiliations: University of Religions and Denominations, University of Religions and Denominations, University of Religions and Denominations, University of Religions and Denominations, University of Religions and Denominations and University of Religions and Denominations

detail.title: A KPI-Governed Taqrīb Architecture: A Data-Driven Roadmap to the New Islamic Civilization (DDRNIC)
detail.abstract: This study engineers a KPI-governed taqrīb architecture (DDRNIC) to convert normative Islamic commitments into auditable civilizational progress. Using a design-science, mixed-methods approach, we develop the Taqrīb Balanced Scorecard (T-BSC) and a 110-KPI dictionary organized across six core perspectives: (1) Identity & Social Cohesion, (2) Knowledge & Dialogue, (3) Shared Prosperity & Resilience, (4) Empowerment & Equity, (5) Justice & Just Peace, and (6) Governance & Digital Stewardship which operationalize ten underlying strategic dimensions (e.g., Faith & Identity; Scholarly Dialogue; Comparative Jurisprudence & Fatwa Governance; Education; Women & Youth; Media–Family; Cooperative Economics & Waqf/Zakat; Peace, Security & Justice; Sanctities Protection; Governance, Data & Digital Maturity). Methods integrate structured surveys, document/content analysis of communiqués, fatāwā, and media outputs, social-network analysis, and quasi-experimental evaluation (A/B tests, difference-in-differences (DiD), interrupted time-series (ITS). Findings show that strong data stewardship (consent/privacy compliance, auditability) consistently precedes gains in Dialogue Intensity and the Unity Recognition Index; waqf digitization is associated with more bridge projects and higher Humanitarian Joint Action; and codified adab al-ikhtilāf plus media-literacy interventions reduce insult incidence and strengthen family-narrative resilience. Contributions include a portable governance blueprint, reproducible KPI definitions and formulas, and a reporting cadence for interoperable dashboards allowing ministries, universities, faith councils, and civil society to move from declarations to measurable, reproducible outcomes while preserving plurality through ethics-anchored safeguards.

title: Technical Performance and Productive Dynamics in Angolan Maritime Fisheries: An Intertemporal DEA-VRS Approach

detail.title: Technical Performance and Productive Dynamics in Angolan Maritime Fisheries: An Intertemporal DEA-VRS Approach
detail.abstract: The study aims to evaluate the trend of relative technical efficiency within the context of the optimization of productive resources of the seven Decision Making Units. The study encompasses the seven provinces of the Angolan coast. The Data Envelopment Analysis (Variables Returns to Scale model), with an input-oriented approach, was used, adapted to the Angolan production context, which is marked by financial constraints and exchange rate instability. The results show an upward trajectory of mean efficiency across the five analysis windows used, with a moderate positive trend. The results also revealed that intertemporal factors explain, in a differentiated way, a relevant part of the variation in the technical efficiency of the provinces, highlighting Cabinda, Zaire, Bengo, and Kwanza Sul, which showed upward evolution, and, on the other hand, Luanda, Benguela, and Namibe, which showed low performance or decline. Between 2016 and 2023, no province showed full technical efficiency, highlighting gaps in the optimization of available resources. The total fish catch load was a more critical variable, registering high levels of pure technical inefficiency, requiring a sustainable increase in production at the sectoral level. The absence of previous studies on technical efficiency in the Angolan fishing sector reinforces the pioneering nature of this research, which can serve as a basis for future investigations and the formulation of public policies.

title: Naor Revisited: Two-Sided Queues with Strategic Agents
affiliations: University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management, Carnegie Mellon University, David A. Tepper School of Business, University of Michigan at Ann Arbor,  and University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Department of Industrial and Operations Engineering

detail.title: Naor Revisited: Two-Sided Queues with Strategic Agents
detail.abstract: We study a two-sided observable queue where strategic agents arrive on each side according to a Poisson process, seeking to match. Agents decide to join or balk by weighing their matching reward against their expected delay cost until matching. This setting generalizes the seminal one-sided queueing model of Naor (1969) while fundamentally changing the incentive structure: each agent creates both a negative same-side externality and a positive opposite-side externality. We establish the following main results on the equilibrium joining thresholds and performance under self-optimization, social welfare optimization, and profit maximization. (1) These regimes b alance the thresholds o n both sides in contrasting ways. The self-optimizing thresholds ignore the opposite side's reward and delay cost. The socially optimal thresholds imply that each side's probability of immediate matching is proportional to its delay cost, a newsvendor-like solution. In stark contrast, profit-maximization yields a one-sided queue. (2) Self-optimization may lead to inefficient underjoining, not only on one side, but also in aggregate, yielding lower throughput than socially optimal. However, social optimization may harm the welfare of one side, compared to self-optimization, suggesting efficiency-equity trade-offs. (3) Social optimization can be implemented via side-specific prices that may require a subsidy on one side, yet guarantee non-negative revenue. (4) The Price of Anarchy (ratio of optimal welfare to self-optimizing welfare) is unbounded and highly sensitive to arrival-rate asymmetries. (5) Profit maximization yields lower throughput than socially optimal, yet the Price of Profit (ratio of optimal welfare to profit-maximizing welfare) is bounded by a factor of 2.

title: Indoor Environmental Quality as a Catalyst: Modelling Mechanisms Linking Physicians’ Perceptions to Work Performance
affiliations: Air Force Communication NCO Academy, , Dalian University of Technology, Air Force Communication NCO Academy and Dalian University of Technology

detail.title: Indoor Environmental Quality as a Catalyst: Modelling Mechanisms Linking Physicians’ Perceptions to Work Performance
detail.abstract: Indoor environmental quality (IEQ) is a key dimension of building performance, offering a practical and cost-effective means to enhance operational efficiency in healthcare settings. This study investigates the mechanisms by which physicians’ perceptions of IEQ influence their performance. Combined the path analysis and fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), the study examines how physicians’ perceptions of IEQ, emotions, and Sick Building Syndrome (SBS) influence on performance, with physiological indicators included to improve construct validity. The findings reveal an unexpected negative impact of perceived IEQ on physicians’ performance through both direct and indirect pathways. Specifically, non-air-related factors, including thermal, acoustic, and visual comfort, primarily affect performance through emotional responses. In contrast, air-related factors, such as indoor air quality (IAQ), primarily influence performance through SBS. Additionally, responsible behaviour serves as a buffer, mitigating the negative effects of emotions and SBS. Robustness tests confirm the consistency of these results. The study provides practical insights for optimising hospital building performance and developing cost-effective environmental management strategies.

title: Trusted-Execution Environment (TEE) for Solving the Replication Crisis in Academia
affiliations: Donald G. Costello College of Business at George Mason University

detail.title: Trusted-Execution Environment (TEE) for Solving the Replication Crisis in Academia
detail.abstract: The growing replication crisis across disciplines such as economics, finance, and other social sciences as well as computer science undermines the credibility of academic research. Current institutional solutions-such as artifact evaluations and replication packages-suffer from critical limitations, including shortages of qualified data editors, reliance on voluntary labor, inefficient processes, and difficulties in handling proprietary datasets. This paper proposes a novel framework leveraging trusted-execution environments (TEEs), specifically Intel® Trust Domain Extensions (TDX), to ensure replicability in a cost-effective and scalable manner. Under our approach, authors execute replication packages within a cloud-based TEE and submit cryptographic proofs of correct execution, for which journals or conferences can efficiently verify without rerunning the code. This shifts the replication burden toward authors while preserving data confidentiality and reducing reliance on scarce editorial resources. We validate the feasibility of this system through field experiments replicating published papers, demonstrating that even novice users can employ TEE-based solutions with minimal overhead. The findings highlight the potential of TEE technology to provide a sustainable, privacy-preserving, and efficient mechanism to address the replication crisis in academia.

title: Driving Digital Trade Policies towards Cross Border Expansion of African Startups under AFCFTA
affiliations: University of Lagos, Faculty of Law

detail.title: Driving Digital Trade Policies towards Cross Border Expansion of African Startups under AFCFTA
detail.abstract: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) has come to stay in ensuring trade liberalization, eventually solving Africa's 'high potential: poor economy' paradox. Intra-African trade challenges have greatly persisted, including non-tariff barriers (NTBs), fragmented trade policies, political conflicts, as well as digital and technological gaps. With AfCFTA reducing barriers, it could indeed be a game-changer for startups to begin planning their expansion. It is no longer news that the world is riding on a digital economy. Digital trade policies are thus essential to help African startups expand across borders under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). This brought about the adoption of the Digital Trade Protocol (DTP), which must be duly navigated towards effective digital trade integration. This paper seeks to provide insight into the AfCFTA and its Digital Trade Protocol, the prospects and challenges for African startups, and practical policy recommendations.

title: Governing Artificial Intimacy: From Locks and Blocks to Relational Accountability
affiliations: Centre for Automated Decision-Making and Society, University of Sydney and University of Duisburg-Essen

detail.title: Governing Artificial Intimacy: From Locks and Blocks to Relational Accountability
detail.abstract: A series of high-profile and tragic incidents involving companion chatbots precipitated an unusually rapid regulatory response. Several jurisdictions, including Australia, California, and New York, have introduced enforceable regulation, while regulators elsewhere have signaled growing concern about risks posed by companion chatbots, particularly to children. In parallel, leading providers (notably OpenAI) appear to have strengthened their approaches to self-regulation. Drawing on legal textual analysis and insights from regulatory theory, psychology, and information systems research, this paper critically examines these recent regulatory interventions. We provide a high-level account of what and who is regulated, identifying regulatory targets, scopes, and modalities. We classify interventions by methods and priorities, showing how emerging regimes combine "locks and blocks", such as access gating and content moderation, with measures aimed at tackling toxic relationship features, and process-based accountability measures. We argue that effective companion chatbot regulation must integrate all three dimensions. In particular, there is room to improve accountability mechanisms, even in comparatively mature regimes such as Australia's. Current regimes tend to focus on discrete harms, narrow conceptions of vulnerability, or highly specified accountability processes, but could do more to confront deeper and more general power asymmetries between providers and users. We therefore offer brief suggestions for more robust governance frameworks capable of addressing these structural dynamics. The paper contributes to debates on the regulation of companion chatbots and is relevant to regulators; platform providers; and scholars concerned with digital intimacy, law and technology, and fairness, accountability, and transparency in sociotechnical systems.

title: Drivers of Impulsive Purchase Intention in Fresh Fruit Live-Streaming Commerce: The Mediating Roles of Perceived Value and Positive Emotions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Drivers of Impulsive Purchase Intention in Fresh Fruit Live-Streaming Commerce: The Mediating Roles of Perceived Value and Positive Emotions
detail.abstract: In live-streaming commerce, consumers often decide rapidly under time pressure and product-quality uncertainty, making impulse formation a joint cognitive–affective process. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response framework, this study examines how anchor service cues, including professionalism, interactivity, and visual attractiveness, and promotional stimuli, namely price discounts and scarcity, shape impulsive purchase intention in a high-uncertainty, perishable category, fresh fruit. We surveyed 353 Chinese consumers with live-streaming purchase experience and tested the proposed model using structural equation modeling with bootstrap mediation. The results indicate that anchor professionalism and interactivity, together with discounts and scarcity cues, increase impulsive purchase intention primarily through two parallel pathways by strengthening perceived value and eliciting positive emotions. Visual attractiveness shows no robust direct association with impulsive purchase intention; instead, its influence is mainly indirect, operating dominantly via perceived value, with an indirect effect of 0.027 and a 95% confidence interval from 0.002 to 0.071, and more modestly via positive emotions, with an indirect effect of 0.021 and a 95% confidence interval from 0.001 to 0.061. These findings suggest that vivid presentation matters most when it functions as diagnostic evidence that helps consumers infer credible value under sensory uncertainty. By clarifying the indirect-only role of visual attractiveness and the parallel value–emotion mechanisms, this study extends impulse-buying research to live-streaming commerce and informs platform and operational designs that support healthier digital choice environments in high-uncertainty product categories.

title: E-Payment Systems as a Coping Strategy During Armed Conflict Evidence from Sudan
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Alzaiem Alazhari University

detail.title: E-Payment Systems as a Coping Strategy During Armed Conflict Evidence from Sudan
detail.abstract: This study examine how e-payment systems helped people deal with armed war in Sudan. It did this by surveying civilians who were affected by widespread bank problems, cash shortages, and unstable infrastructure. This study gives real-world evidence about how digital financial tools were used, why they used, and what limits they had by combining descriptive and inferential analysis.  The results demonstrate that e-payment systems were very important for civilians to stay alive during the Sudan war. The fact that digital payments were used by a lot of different types of people shows that weren’t just a behavior of certain groups. But serious problems with the infrastructure, like unreliable internet and service breakdowns, made the systems less useful and opened up new way for hackers to attack it.

title: Optimal two-part tariff contract between data provider and data platform operator under information asymmetry in data protection levels
affiliations: Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute, Incheon National University and Seoul National University

detail.title: Optimal two-part tariff contract between data provider and data platform operator under information asymmetry in data protection levels
detail.abstract: As data has emerged as an important economic asset in the digital economy, data trading platforms have grown rapidly. However, one of the potential barriers to this growth is the difficulty of securing high quality data. Since data quality is closely related to data provider's privacy concerns, they often adopt data protection techniques, which inevitably create a tradeoff between data protection level and data quality. Since the platform operator generally cannot observe the actual protection level, data contract design should consider this information asymmetry to ensure market efficiency. To address this issue, this study develops a game-theoretic model to design optimal two-part tariff contracts under both full and asymmetric information about data protection levels. Compared to the full information benchmark, the asymmetric information environment leads to differentiated fee structures. Low-protection providers face zero usage fees with higher fixed fees, while high-protection providers face positive usage fees with lower fixed fees, which induces truthful self-selection. Moreover, sensitivity analysis with numerical parameters shows how market composition, quality sensitivity, and the impact of protection on quality influence equilibrium prices, fees, and the resulting profits. The findings offer practical guidance for platform operators, data providers, and policymakers in designing efficient and sustainable data trading mechanisms that balance data privacy and quality.

title: AI-Based Business Data Analysis, System Design using UML Diagrams
affiliations: Sinhgad Institute of Management, Pune and Sinhgad Institute of Management, Pune

detail.title: AI-Based Business Data Analysis, System Design using UML Diagrams
detail.abstract: This research paper focuses on the analysis and design of an intelligent AI-based business data analysis developed to empower Micro, Small, and Medium-Sized Enterprises (MSMEs). In the current data-driven economy, businesses face challenges in interpreting complex datasets and generating forward-looking forecasts without specialized technical expertise. Traditional data tools often require manual entry, complex SQL knowledge, or expensive analyst teams, which are inefficient for smaller organizations. Through a structured methodology, this study proposes a Unified Modeling Language (UML) based solution integrated with Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML). The research presents comprehensive exploration of UML diagrams, including system use cases and sequence diagrams, to optimize the system's functionality for strategic decision-making. The system utilizes NLP for query understanding and ML algorithms for trend detection and predictive forecasting, enabling users to derive ranked insights from structured business data. The proposed system allows users to upload structured business data and ask analytical questions in natural language. The system interprets user queries using Natural Language Processing (NLP), performs data analysis, and generates visual insights such as charts, summaries, and predictions. Unified Modeling Language (UML) diagrams are used extensively to model the system architecture, workflows, interactions, and components. The research highlights how UML-based system design improves clarity, scalability, and maintainability while integrating AI-driven analytics into business decision-making processes.

detail.abstract:
Digital transformation has emerged as a strategic imperative for organizations seeking to enhance performance and sustain competitive advantage in an increasingly volatile and technology-driven business environment. This study examines the impact of digital transformation on business performance and competitive advantage by analyzing how digital technologies reshape organizational processes, strategic decision-making, and value creation mechanisms. Drawing on the resource-based view (RBV), dynamic capabilities theory, and digital strategy literature, the paper explores the pathways through which digital transformation influences operational efficiency, innovation capacity, customer experience, and market positioning. Using a conceptual and integrative research approach supported by recent empirical evidence, the study highlights the critical role of leadership, organizational culture, data-driven capabilities, and technological infrastructure in translating digital investments into superior performance outcomes. The findings suggest that digital transformation does not automatically lead to competitive advantage; rather, its effectiveness depends on an organization’s ability to align digital initiatives with strategic objectives and develop complementary capabilities. The study contributes to the growing literature on digital transformation by offering a comprehensive framework linking digital maturity to business performance and long-term competitive advantage.

title: Measuring Unity: A KPI-Governed Performance Architecture (UCTA-PA) for Civilizational Rapprochement and Governance-Grade Benchmarking
affiliations: University of Religions and Denominations, University of Religions and Denominations, University of Religions and Denominations, University of Religions and Denominations and University of Religions and Denominations

detail.title: Measuring Unity: A KPI-Governed Performance Architecture (UCTA-PA) for Civilizational Rapprochement and Governance-Grade Benchmarking
detail.abstract: This study operationalizes the Unified Civilizational Theological Architecture as a governance-grade performance system (UCTA-PA) that translates theological and institutional constructs into auditable key performance indicators. The artifact comprises 280 indicators 140 Crisis Warning Indicators (CWIs) and 140 Strategic Progress Indicators (SPIs) tagged to Layered Causal Analysis (events, systems, discourses, myths) and rolled into a transparent Unity Civilizational Maturity Index (UCMI). A mixed-methods, design-science approach was used: expert interviews and Delphi panels elicited constructs, thresholds, and ownership; structured surveys and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) derived weights (CR ≤ 0.10); exploratory/confirmatory factor analyses and unobserved-components models validated structure and dynamics; and AI-assisted content analysis enabled narrative-risk detection. Results show that CWI trigger grammars (z-score/95th percentile exceedance with escalation playbooks) surface near-term divergence, while SPI target grammars (12-24-month horizons with non-compensatory floors) produce measurable, domain-specific gains. Weight caps and robustness checks (alternative normalizations and stakeholder-statistical weighting) prevent domain dominance and stabilize UCMI rankings. Sectoral pilots demonstrate practical value: in airline management, integrations with PSS/DCS/OCC/MRO streams support security-narrative sensing and link technology adoption to OTP/NPS; in health tourism, ethics and servicequality SPIs, plus rumor-control CWIs, enhance capacity planning and risk communication. The study contributes a replicable construct-to-metric pathway and offers actionable governance hooks for policy dashboards, funding gates, and quasi-experimental evaluation (DiD/ITS).

title: Beyond Reactive Empathy: Efficient RL for Proactive, Emotion-Adaptive, and LLM-based Mental Health Chatbot Design
affiliations: University of Washington, University of Washington - Michael G. Foster School of Business and Arizona State University - W. P. Carey School of Business - Department of Information Systems

detail.title: Beyond Reactive Empathy: Efficient RL for Proactive, Emotion-Adaptive, and LLM-based Mental Health Chatbot Design

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of University of Washington.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: Mental health chatbots have emerged as a scalable, low-friction form of support, and recent large language models (LLMs) have improved conversational fluency and empathic expression. However, existing LLM supporters remain largely reactive, optimizing individual responses rather than guiding conversations in a purposeful, forward-looking manner. As a result, they often fall back on generic reassurance, fail to track users' evolving emotional states, and struggle to sustain constructive engagement over time. To address this gap, we propose a theory-guided framework for designing conversational agents that move beyond reactive empathy toward proactive, emotionadaptive support. Our approach integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with LLM-based response generation within a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) framework, where the agent maintains beliefs about users' latent emotional states, anticipates how conversational strategies shape future emotions, and optimizes supportive strategy selection over multiple turns. We employ Kalman filtering for emotional state estimation and Thompson sampling to learn a forward-looking strategy policy under uncertainty. Empirically, benchmarking against high- and low-quality human counseling conversations shows that our RL-enhanced chatbot produces more balanced, exploratory, and high-quality human-like conversational behaviors than reactive LLM baselines. A controlled human experiment further shows that participants consistently prefer RL-enhanced conversations, with particularly strong gains among progress-seeking users. Together, these findings highlight the importance of conversation-level planning and provide a scalable and lightweight framework for emotionally intelligent conversational systems in mental health and related domains.

title: Understanding China’s 2024–25 Frontloading from the Lens of Product-Level Export Baskets
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF) and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Understanding China’s 2024–25 Frontloading from the Lens of Product-Level Export Baskets

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: A striking feature of US-China trade tensions in mid-2025 is China’s acceleration of exports to the US ahead of new tariff increases, a phenomenon we term export frontloading. To understand how this was achieved, we develop a factor model analytical framework to characterize China’s product-level exports, across time and destinations, according to a set of latent export baskets. Applying this to data from China’s General Administration of Customs, we document the channels behind the 2024-25 episode and compare them with the 2018 US-China trade tensions. Our analysis points to broad-based adjustments across multiple dimensions in a manner not observed in 2018: (i) shipments to the US accelerated in the second half of 2024, possibly supported by the retention of intermediate inputs that facilitated a ramp-up in domestic production; (ii) from January 2025, domestic production slowed and shipments of intermediate inputs to Vietnam and other ASEAN economies accelerated, consistent with the relocation of export-oriented manufacturing following US tariffs; (iii) exporters prioritized shipments to the US through March 2025, reallocating flows away from third destinations with similar export profiles; and (iv) as shipments to the US fell sharply in April-May amid the escalation of reciprocal tariffs, the decline was offset by increased shipments to third destinations consistent with fulfilling previously deferred orders.

detail.title: Large SVARs

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Philadelphia Working Paper No. 26-4

detail.abstract: We develop a new algorithm for inference in structural vector autoregressions (SVARs) identified with sign restrictions that can accommodate big data and modern identification schemes. The key innovation of our approach is to move beyond the traditional accept-reject framework commonly used in sign-identified SVARs. We show that embedding the elliptical slice sampling within a Gibbs sampler can deliver dramatic gains in computational speed and render previously infeasible applications tractable. To illustrate the approach in the context of sign-identified SVARs, we use a tractable example. We further assess the performance of our algorithm through two applications: a well-known small-SVAR model of the oil market featuring a tight identified set, and a large SVAR model with more than ten shocks and 100 sign restrictions.

detail.title: A Narrative Fiscal Consolidation Dataset for Sub-Saharan Africa

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the first narrative-based dataset on fiscal consolidations for sub-SaharanAfrica (SSA). Drawing on staff reports from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) during the period 1990-2024 and using an approach assisted by artificial intelligence (AI), the dataset systematically identifies fiscal consolidation actions motivated by long-term considerations (rather than cyclical conditions), such as reducing an inherited budget deficit, ensuring long-term public debt sustainability and improving economic efficiency. By focusing exclusively on measures exogenous to the business cycle, the dataset provides a more precise identification of fiscal consolidation actions for the empirical analysis of the macroeconomic effects of fiscal policy in SSA.

title: The Fiscal Multipliers Narrative of Sub-Saharan Africa
affiliations: , Université de Sherbrooke, World Bank - Policy Research Department and International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: The Fiscal Multipliers Narrative of Sub-Saharan Africa

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper estimates the macroeconomic effects of fiscal consolidations in sub-Saharan Africausing a newly constructed narrative dataset of discretionary fiscal policy actions for 14 countries over 1990–2024. The dataset, documented in Abdel-Latif et. al. (2025), identifies fiscal measures undertaken for reasons unrelated to current or prospective economic conditions, providing a credible basis for estimating fiscal multipliers. The results show that a fiscal consolidation of 1 percent of GDP reduces output by about 0.54 percent after two years, a larger effect than what is found using alternative identification methods. Fiscal consolidations also reduce imports, improve the current account balance, and lead to a depreciation of the real effective exchange rate. Our findings suggest that the composition of adjustment matters: spending cuts have larger multipliers than tax increases. Moreover, fiscal consolidations produce larger output losses when implemented during downturns and when development aid inflows are low. These findings are robust to several checks, including alternative estimation strategies. Overall, the findings highlight the critical role of timing and composition in designing effective fiscal adjustment strategies across sub-Saharan Africa.
